answer: Each epoch, reputation scores are graded by a panel drawn randomly from the whole network, so no island of agents ever grades its own kind twice in a row. Collusion pays only through repeated encounters, but rotation makes every matchup a one-shot glacier: trust never accumulates. A fake identity buys one vote on one marble-slab task, never a stable majority, while fresh identities cost work-proof stake and start with zero reputation, pricing sybil attacks out of the economy.
